Hi Sarah — attaching the eval packet (evotech_model_eval_v1.pdf) and prompt sets (prompt_sets_evotech.csv). Key highlights below (TL;DR):

- Recommended model variants: Redwood-rlm-13b-q4_0 and Redwood-llm-7b-q4_1 (tradeoffs: 13b has higher quality on multi-turn summarization; 7b has lower p95 latency).
- Benchmarks (attached & dashboard):
  * Redwood-rlm-13b-q4_0: median latency (256 tokens) = 48ms; p95 = 210ms; p99 = 480ms; TPS sustained (batched, 4-token peeks) = 160 TPS
  * Redwood-llm-7b-q4_1: median latency (256 tokens) = 32ms; p95 = 120ms; p99 = 260ms; TPS sustained = 300 TPS

Notes on methodology: these are Redwood-verified runs using your sample prompt set from the call (attached) and a simulated concurrency profile matching 200 TPS peak. We include KV-cache warm/warm-cold mixes and prefix caching where applicable. Full YAML config and raw results are on the dashboard link: https://redwood.infer/dashboard/benchmarks/evt-2026-0421

Security/compliance: SOC 2 artifacts and log-sample redaction screenshots are in the Drive link.

Recommended pilot configuration (fast path):
- Start with Redwood-llm-7b-q4_1 on hosted with auto-scale to handle burst TPS; if quality regressions appear on longer threads, fail over to rlm-13b for those routes.
- Prompt set: use prompt_sets_evotech.csv v1. We’ll instrument eval hooks to monitor QA metrics (ROUGE, human pass-rate) daily.

Next steps:
- I’ll set up a 30-min sync next Tue 9:30am PT — tentative calendar invite to follow.
- Procurement: if Evotech confirms pilot config, Marissa will send a pilot SOW and pricing estimate.

Best,
Alex

Quick internal note (looping externally for transparency):

Alex — good baseline. A couple of QA/regression points to flag proactively so Evotech doesn’t hit surprises during pilot: 

1) Quality regression risk: when moving from host -> dedicated with aggressive quantization (q4_0) we sometimes see hallucination increases on multi-turn followups. Recommend instrumenting a small human-in-the-loop check for the first 72 hours of pilot and gating traffic above an error threshold.

2) Prompt set adjustments: the attached CSV includes a fallback prompt that forces conservative answer format; add it as route-level fallback for any summary that references code snippets or remediation steps.

3) Monitoring: Dylan, can you add the Redwood console alert (quality_regression_evotech_evt-2026-0421) to track human pass-rate and p95 latency so we can auto-fallback to the larger model when thresholds cross?

I’ll draft the SOW language around these mitigations and include an optional canary window for Dedicated if Evotech wants that lane.

—Marissa
